newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key March JGB futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: Key March JGB futures end lower.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Wednesday's Tokyo session down on position-adjustment selling.
March closed down 0.30 at 125.30, after falling as low as 125.19 in the morning. Volume was 44,420 contracts.
The Tokyo stock market's strong rebound, though seen supportive for JGBs at this stage, failed to encourage buying today, traders said.
The key Nikkei 225 average ended up 387.70 points or 2.02 percent at 19,549.41, after falling 529 points or 2.69 percent on Tuesday.
"JGBs failed to move in line with stocks today as they were capped by position-adjustment selling ahead of the year-end," said a brokerage house trader.
Traders said JGBs could show further weakness if stocks resume their downtrend.

"Depending on stock price moves, we may see further weakness in JGBs. The yield of the benchmark cash JGB may rise above 2.50 percent if the Nikkei falls below 19,000. However, some bargain-hunting from investors is likely to emerge if the benchmark yield rises to 2.50 percent," said a trader at another brokerage house.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB stood at 2.450 percent, up from 2.415 percent on Tuesday.
Traders said the upside was heavy due to sluggish sentiment carried over from the previous day.
JGBs fell sharply on Tuesday after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) reduced the amount of outright bond purchase to 100 billion yen from the usual 200 billion yen in its morning operations.
Market players will be nervously watching the BOJ's outright bond purchase operations in January to see if the central bank will continue to reduce the amount of its bond buying, traders said.

The BOJ so far this year had been conducting outright JGB purchase operations twice a month, buying 200 billion yen worth each time until it surprised the market by offering to buy only 100 billion yen worth on Tuesday.
A BOJ official said on Tuesday that the decision to cut the amount of outright bond purchase was due to an easing of the year-end fund shortage and a slowdown in bank note growth.
Some traders, however, suspect the bank may be trying to discourage long-term interest rates from falling further.
On Thursday, the market is likely to focus on Japan's industrial production data for November, traders said.

"There is a lingering impact from the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) move to cut its outright bond purchases earlier in the week. Players are nervous about carrying over positions into the new year, so they are squaring up," a brokerage house trader said.
The BOJ surprised the market on Tuesday by offering to buy only 100 billion yen worth of bonds outright, half the usual amount of 200 billion yen.
Market players will be nervously watching the BOJ's outright bond purchase operations in January to see if the bank will continue to reduce the amount of its bond buying, traders said.
Traders said market participants are also nervous about the yen/dollar rate.
The dollar rose against the yen to over 115 yen in Tokyo at mid-morning, its highest level in over 44 months.

In the afternoon, the market will be focusing on BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's appearance before a parliamentary panel from about 2 p.m. (0500 GMT) and the release of Japan's November industrial production data at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), traders said.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
